A23-65 + A23-74 (user 2026-10-07): while walking in any direction but a backpedal toward the camera (walk . look < -0.35) the camera turns toward the walk (eased; the cap is 45 deg/s within 20 deg of the camera look, fading smoothly to 16 deg/s by 60 deg, so camera-relative W+D / D / a 37-100 deg stick walk wide arcs, radius >= 55 studs at WalkSpeed 20; 25 / 10 deg/s with 'Screen shake' off or Reduced Motion); 0.25 s after the walk ends the camera eases round behind the HumanoidRootPart's facing (ease in, <= 120 deg/s, ease out; D or W+D let go -> within 8 deg in 1.2 s, then within 1 deg, no overshoot; a 6 deg dead zone keeps it still once behind; 60 deg/s with 'Screen shake' off or Reduced Motion); never after a backpedal (no 180 deg spin), for a dead character, or after a hand turn within 1.5 s before the stop or any time after it (kept until the next walk); the phone thumbstick drives it, its touch never holds it; neither turn 1.5 s after a right drag / camera-side finger drag / right stick, 0.5 s after my own Swing / Release / Skill Fx (the recenter resumes after it), in shift lock, first person, a window / scripted camera, or with Settings Camera = Free. Review A23-74 (user 2026-10-07): Roblox's own keyboard / trackpad camera turn (Left / Right arrows, Comma / Period held or tapped, processed or not, outside a text box; a trackpad pan, not a wheel / pinch zoom) is a hand turn too (a held Right arrow turned 14 deg and snapped back before); the walking cap is never above speed / 55 studs (speed = Humanoid WalkSpeed x how far the stick is pushed), so a stick held anywhere 0..110 deg off forward walks a circle of radius >= 50 studs (55 at 20-35 deg; 38 before); Start sets LocalPlayer.DevTouchCameraMode = Classic when it is UserChoice / Follow (the place's StarterPlayer DevTouchCameraMovementMode is UserChoice, so phones got Roblox's Follow camera and its own walking turn: 10-stud circles at a 90 deg stick), and while Roblox's Follow camera is still active (the set refused, a PC player who picked Follow) WalkTurn stays off (the standing recenter still runs); a frame is clamped to 1/20 s (a 0.5 s hitch turned the recenter 60 deg, now <= 6).
limitations: Engine input propagation, the default camera's right-drag orbit itself and real mouse/touch need runtime validation (Studio own test Play).
